title: Hydrogen lines constrain a stated atomic model
question: What can a hydrogen spectrum establish about atomic structure?
answerPreview: A calibrated line can constrain level differences in a declared hydrogen-like Hamiltonian model, but it does not reveal a unique structure or transition strength by inspection.
summary: Connect hydrogen-like level differences to photon energy, cyclic frequency, and vacuum wavelength while declaring reduced mass, transition assumptions, selection-rule limits, and omitted corrections.

guidedBlocks.title: A line constrains a declared model
body: The activity selects a one-electron ion, an upper principal level, a lower principal level, and a nuclear-mass option. It then calculates one positive level difference.
That difference has linked photon representations: energy E, cyclic frequency nu, and vacuum wavelength lambda. Changing representation does not create three independent measurements.

Agreement with a calibrated line could constrain this model only after line identification, calibration, uncertainty, and alternatives are stated. This source activity performs none of those empirical steps.

guidedBlocks.title: A moving nucleus changes the scale
body: An infinitely heavy nucleus leaves the electron mass as the orbital mass scale. A finite proton moves too, so the two-body problem uses the reduced mass mu = m_e m_p/(m_e + m_p).
Because mu/m_e is slightly below one, the finite-proton option lowers the effective Rydberg value and transition energy and increases the vacuum wavelength relative to the infinite-mass option.
For atomic number above one, assigning the proton mass is only an illustrative engine choice, not a realistic isotope model.

guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: Reduced-mass correction to the hydrogen-like Rydberg relation
caveats: The engine has no isotope catalog or recoil correction beyond this reduced-mass factor.

guidedBlocks.title: An energy difference is not a selection rule
body: Principal levels identify a possible energy difference but do not specify orbital angular momentum, spin, polarization, or transition matrix elements.
The explorer therefore does not claim that every listed difference is allowed, strong, or observed.
Fine structure, hyperfine structure, Lamb shifts, finite nuclear size, external fields, broadening, and medium response are outside this activity.

technicalBlocks.title: The spectrum requires a Hamiltonian
body: The nonrelativistic point-Coulomb Hamiltonian supplies the bound states whose level differences lead to the Rydberg expression. Dimensional consistency alone cannot determine the discrete 1/n^2 structure or its state labels.
The explorer uses the Bohr/Rydberg result as a conventional model contract; it does not solve an eigenvalue problem at runtime.
Changing the Hamiltonian or adding perturbations can split or shift lines, so a spectrum constrains a specified family of models rather than revealing a unique Hamiltonian.

technicalBlocks.title: The Rydberg baseline has a bounded domain
body: The engine models a nonrelativistic one-electron point-Coulomb system with atomic number from 1 through 10 and principal levels up to 12.

A finite-proton mass is physically appropriate for ordinary hydrogen but only illustrative for higher atomic number. Nuclear charge radius, isotope mass, radiative corrections, and environmental shifts require additional model terms and data.
A measured spectrum also requires instrument calibration, resolution, line-shape modeling, uncertainty, and competing assignments before comparison.
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Atomic engine bounds and Chapter 7 inference limits
caveats: No empirical residual or uncertainty budget is computed.

equationSteps.label: Electron-proton reduced mass
equationSteps.expression: mu = m_e m_p/(m_e + m_p); R_H = R_inf mu/m_e
equationSteps.explanation: The finite-proton factor is below one; the infinite-nuclear-mass option sets mu/m_e to one.
caveats: Higher-order recoil and isotope-specific masses are omitted.

equationSteps.label: Hydrogen-like transition
equationSteps.explanation: The positive wavenumber gives the model vacuum wavelength for the selected downward level difference.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022 R_inf; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Rydberg level-difference relation; OpenStax sections 6.4 and 8.1
caveats: The equation does not assert transition probability or observation.

equationSteps.label: Linked photon representations
equationSteps.expression: nu = c/lambda; E = h nu = h c/lambda
equationSteps.explanation: Energy, cyclic frequency, and vacuum wavelength are derived representations of the same selected level difference.
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Fixed h and c; photon relations
caveats: The wavelength is in vacuum and no refractive index is applied.
